notes: Access: direct HTTP GET (curl, desktop UA), no block encountered. robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow and does not block /c/* or /browse/*. Site is a Vue/Nuxt SSR app (article.com); every listing page server-renders its own exact total in a 'Showing N of TOTAL' string plus a matching 'count' field in the embedded JSON grid data - used as evidence throughout. Navigation discovery: parsed the full mega-nav JSON embedded in the SSR HTML (221 nav entries, identical across /c/best-sellers, /browse/100/new, /c/sale, confirming it is the shared site-wide nav) plus category_sitemap.xml/collection_sitemap.xml/landingpage_sitemap.xml/tag_sitemap.xml from sitemap.xml. Header nav has an explicit 'Best Sellers' entry (id=best-sellers -> /c/best-sellers, labelled 'All Best Sellers') with one genuine child, an 'Outdoor' Best Sellers listing (id=best-sellers-outdoor -> /c/outdoor-bestsellers, also cross-linked from the Outdoor mega-menu as 'Best Sellers'). No other room/category-specific Best Sellers pages exist in the nav (checked every nav id/url pair for 'bestseller'/'best-seller'/'popular'/'trending'/'favorite' - only Pro-only 'Shop Pro Member Favorites' matched separately, which is a B2B trade-account section, not a consumer merchandising PLP, and was excluded). landingpage_sitemap.xml and tag_sitemap.xml also surfaced softer signals (/l/best-sellers, /l/sofa-best-sellers, /l/top-sellers, /l/most-popular-products, /l/trade-favorites, /tag/225/best-sellers, /tag/296/crowd-favorites) but these are legacy Contentful landing/tag pages not present in the live header nav or footer, superseded by the two canonical PLPs below, so not opened individually. Both candidate URLs were opened and confirmed to be real product grids (filterable/sortable, with an exact site-reported count), not editorial pages, and no product-page 'Bestseller' badge was mistaken for a PLP. Did not use site search (/search?*) because robots.txt explicitly disallows it (Disallow: /search?*) and navigation/sitemap discovery already positively confirmed both listings, so a search check was unnecessary per the brief's own absence-proof guidance.
